sections.h2: Which Novi offices send and collect the property tax bill?
sections.html:
Novi's own Treasurer's Office mails and collects the bills, while the city Assessing Department supplies the values behind them. The treasurer works from 45175 Ten Mile Road, Novi, MI 48375, and answers tax questions at 248-347-0440. The Treasurer page also links the online property and tax search.

Novi sits in Oakland County, about 25 miles northwest of downtown Detroit, and covers roughly 30 square miles of land around Walled Lake. I-96, I-696, I-275 and M-5 all reach the city, and the population rose from about 9,700 in 1970 to 66,243 in 2020. Novi became a city in 1969, after starting life as a township in 1832.

The city is only the collecting agent for most of what appears on the statement. Its own operating taxes are billed in full on the summer statement, while the winter statement carries the county, school and authority levies. Novi has no say over the county and school rates.

sections.h2: When are Novi property taxes due?
sections.html:
Two payment seasons apply: late summer and winter. The city's 2026 notice said summer bills would be mailed the week of July 1 and that payments had to reach the treasurer on or before August 31 to avoid an automatic penalty. For anyone reading after that date, the winter window is the one to watch.

Novi billing calendar, from the city's 2026 summer notice and its winter statement

Summer bill mailedWeek of July 1 (2026 notice)Call the treasurer if nothing arrives by July 15
Summer deadlineAugust 31 (2026 notice)Postmarks and post-dated checks are not accepted

After February 14Late period3% automatic penalty that the treasurer cannot waive

A drop box sits behind the Civic Center, and the 2026 notice accepted drop box payments until midnight on the deadline day. Online payment by credit card or electronic check is available through cityofnovi.org. Be careful with the bank numbers you type, because a returned payment after the due date draws the penalty.

sections.h2: How does Novi set the taxable value of a house?
sections.html:
The bill rests on taxable value, a figure that normally sits below half of what the house would fetch. The assessor estimates market value as of Tax Day, December 31 of the year before, and the assessed value is about 50% of that. For 2026 the city used a 24-month sales study running from April 1, 2023 to March 31, 2025, covering roughly 2,000 sales.

Taxable value grows more slowly than assessed value. The 2026 inflation rate multiplier is 1.027, so a home that stays with its owner can rise no more than 2.7%, even if neighborhood prices climbed 10%. The city's formula is the prior taxable value, less losses, times the multiplier, plus additions.

  • Taxable value is the lesser of assessed value and capped value.
  • The tax equals taxable value divided by 1,000, times the millage rate.
  • A sale resets the taxable value to the assessed value the following year.
  • Special assessments, trash charges and penalties are added on top.

After you sell, the next owner's bill will probably run higher than yours did. Tell any buyer to look at the assessed value rather than your old bill.

sections.h2: What is the process to appeal a Novi assessment?
sections.html:
Appeals start with the March Board of Review, the sole yearly chance to contest a current value. Hearings begin on the second Monday of March, after the Notice of Assessment goes out in mid February. Petition forms come from the Assessing Department or the city's website, and you make an appointment to appear.

If the board's answer is not acceptable, the next level is the Michigan Tax Tribunal. A residential petition must go to the Tribunal at 611 W. Ottawa St., Lansing, MI 48933 by July 31, and only after you have appeared before the March board. Commercial and industrial appeals to the Tribunal are due May 31. The July and December boards cannot hear value disputes under MCL 211.53b.

Two relief options sit outside the appeal process. Michigan has no age-based property tax break, but Novi offers an annual poverty exemption based on income and assets, which needs Board of Review approval. Owners who qualify can also ask the Treasurer's Office about deferring summer taxes.

sections.h2: What is a Novi tax bill spent on?
sections.html:
On the city's sample winter statement, about 59% of a homestead bill went to education, 30% to the City of Novi and 11% to Oakland County. That split was based on the Novi and OCC district homestead rates, so a parcel in another district will differ. Several school systems reach into the city.

  • Novi Community Schools cover most of the city.
  • Northville Public Schools serve a large part of the south side.
  • Walled Lake Consolidated Schools take in a pocket with two elementary schools.
  • South Lyon Community Schools hold a small western strip.

The statement's other lines include the county parks and recreation levy, the zoo authority, the art institute, Oakland transit and the Huron Clinton Metropolitan Authority. Check the parcel number and school district code on your own bill before you compare it with a neighbor's.

sections.h2: What do federal housing counts show for Novi?
sections.html:
Census QuickFacts lists 67,319 people in Novi for July 2025 and 26,801 households across 2020 to 2024. Owners live in 66.3% of housing units. The typical owned home is valued at $421,900, rent at the middle is $1,747 a month, and household income at the middle is $110,723.

A condo near the I-96 corridor and a lakeside house will sit well apart from those citywide figures. About 29% of residents were born abroad. Health care, automotive suppliers and the retail cluster around Novi Road and I-96 anchor the local economy.

sections.h2: What follows when Novi tax goes unpaid?
sections.html:
After the winter period closes, the balance moves to Oakland County. MCL 211.78a returns taxes still owed on March 1 as delinquent, adding a 4% county fee and interest at 1% for each month. The county treasurer collects from there, and ongoing nonpayment leads into a three-year foreclosure process.

For 2024 and earlier balances, the county's notices name March 31, 2027 as the final day to pay and keep the property. The treasurer's office, at 248-858-0611, offers repayment schedules and referrals. Our Oakland County property tax guide lays out the foreclosure calendar step by step.

sections.h2: What should a Novi seller do about the principal residence exemption?
sections.html:
The exemption takes up to 18 mills of school operating tax off a home you own and occupy. To see it on the summer bill, you had to be both owner and resident by June 1. People who moved in between June 2 and November 1 can claim a winter exemption.

On a sale, send the Assessing Department the rescission form so the exemption ends on the correct date. A seller who has already bought another Michigan residence may keep it on the old house through a conditional rescission, as long as the old house is listed, vacant, unleased and free of business use. Submit that form with the new exemption by June 1 for both bills, or by November 1 for winter only.

sections.h2: How does a Novi sale handle the tax bill?
sections.html:
At closing, the title company splits the current year's tax between seller and buyer and settles any unpaid amount out of your proceeds. Get the present balance from the city treasurer. If any year has moved to Oakland County, buy an official delinquent tax statement through the county's Property Gateway, which sells them to owners and title companies.

A sale can close with tax owing, since the payoff is a line on the seller's settlement statement. The avoidable cost is the late charge: miss the winter deadline and a 3% penalty applies that staff cannot waive. Pay early, and keep both statements for the year of the sale.

faqs.q: When is the winter tax deadline in Novi?
faqs.a: February 14. The winter statement allows payment from December 1 through February 14, and the money has to be physically in the treasurer's hands by that day. A 3% penalty starts after it, and no one at the counter can waive it.

faqs.q: Will a postmark count as on-time in Novi?
faqs.a: No. The city's notices say postmarks and post-dated checks are refused. Use the drop box behind the Civic Center, pay online, or mail the check early enough to arrive on time.

faqs.q: Do taxes rise after buying a Novi house?
faqs.a: Often. The year after a sale, taxable value resets to the assessed value, which may sit well above the earlier capped figure. Later increases are limited to the inflation multiplier or 5%, whichever is smaller.

faqs.q: Which Novi department answers questions about my value?
faqs.a: The Assessing Department handles values, exemptions, and name or address changes. Bills and payments go through the Treasurer's Office at 248-347-0440.

faqs.q: Can a Novi house with tax behind still be sold?
faqs.a: Yes. The title company pays the balance, with penalty and interest, from your proceeds at closing. Request a current statement first from the city, or from the Oakland County Treasurer for earlier years.
